A rebrand and polish release: the project is now **Nivyx**. This is a
product/packaging/CLI-naming milestone, not an engine change — **the
underlying bypass engine (nftables/WinDivert/PF interception,
DNS-over-HTTPS, TLS record fragmentation, the decision ladder, fail-open
behavior) is unchanged from v2.0.0.**

## New name: Nivyx

- Product name: **Nivyx**. Repository, README, docs, installers and
  terminal output are rebranded accordingly.
- New primary CLI command: **`nivyx`** — `nivyx status`, `nivyx
  doctor`, `nivyx logs`, `nivyx restart`, `nivyx diagnose <host>`,
  `nivyx version`, etc. Identical behavior to the previous `dpictl` on
  every platform (Linux, Windows, macOS): same one implementation,
  just a new front-door name.
- **`dpictl` and `dpi-proxy-ctl` are kept as compatibility aliases** —
  every command works the same through any of the three names, and
  existing scripts that call `dpictl` or `dpi-proxy-ctl` keep working
  unchanged. There is no duplicated logic: all three names run the
  same script/binary.
- Renamed double-click installers: `Install Nivyx.cmd` / `Uninstall
  Nivyx.cmd` (Windows), `Install Nivyx.command` / `Uninstall
  Nivyx.command` (macOS). Linux keeps `scripts/install.sh`.
- Renamed release assets: `nivyx-linux-x86_64`,
  `nivyx-windows-x86_64.zip`, `nivyx-macos-arm64.zip`,
  `nivyx-macos-x86_64.zip`, `SHA256SUMS`.

## Platform status: Windows and macOS are no longer Beta

Linux, Windows (10/11, x64) and macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) are
all now **supported** — the "Beta" label is removed. Validation status
is unchanged: all three are end-to-end tested in CI on real runners,
and field-tested against real ISP-level DPI (Windows and macOS each on
one physical machine so far); none of the three has been validated
across a wide range of consumer hardware and networks yet.

## What did *not* change

Internal identifiers that existing installs, upgrades and uninstalls
depend on are kept exactly as they were, to avoid breaking anything
already deployed:

- The installed binary is still named `dpi-proxy` (and
  `dpi-proxy-packet` for optional packet mode).
- systemd unit names (`dpi-proxy-transparent.service`,
  `dpi-proxy-packet.service`), the Windows service name (`dpi-proxy`),
  the macOS launchd label (`io.github.kadireren7.dpi-proxy`) and PF
  anchor (`com.apple/dpi-proxy`), the nftables tables (`inet
  dpi_proxy_tp`, `inet dpi_proxy`), and config/state paths
  (`/etc/dpi-proxy`, `/var/lib/dpi-proxy`, `%ProgramData%\dpi-proxy`,
  …) are all unchanged.
- An existing v2.0.0 install upgrades in place with no manual steps;
  `nivyx` simply becomes available alongside the `dpictl` you already
  had.

## Terminal output polish

- `status` and `doctor` are now colored on a real terminal (green for
  healthy/running, yellow for warnings, red for failures) and stay
  plain text automatically when piped, redirected, or when
  [`NO_COLOR`](https://no-color.org) is set — nothing to configure.
- `nivyx --help` / `nivyx version` print a short, Nivyx-branded
  summary instead of the old `dpi-for-everyone`/`dpi-proxy` banner.

## Branding, docs and assets

- New README with a logo, tagline and badges (build status, latest
  release, license, platforms) — implementation detail dumps stay in
  `docs/`.
- New vector assets: `assets/logo.svg`, `assets/logo-mark.svg`,
  `assets/nivyx-terminal.svg` (a deterministic sample of `nivyx
  status`/`nivyx doctor` output, no personal information).
- `docs/cli.md`, `docs/linux.md`, `docs/windows.md`, `docs/macos.md`,
  `docs/performance.md`, `docs/transparent-mode.md` and the platform
  quick-start files updated to `nivyx` as the primary command, with
  `dpictl`/`dpi-proxy-ctl` documented as compatibility aliases.

## Assets

- `nivyx-linux-x86_64` — Linux binary (install from source with `scripts/install.sh`)
- `nivyx-windows-x86_64.zip` — Windows transparent mode + SOCKS5
- `nivyx-macos-arm64.zip`, `nivyx-macos-x86_64.zip` — macOS transparent mode
- `SHA256SUMS`
